samples.summary: Comment/thread deletion has no author (or manager) authorization check, so any workspace member or write-scoped API key can destroy another user's comments
samples.evidence: `DELETE .../comments/:threadId` (comments.controller.ts:236-249) and `DELETE .../comments/:threadId/comments/:commentId` (comments.controller.ts:252-281) authorize on nothing but workspace membership (`loadCommentableType` → `getDocumentOrThrow`) plus, for API keys, the `write` scope. Neither compares `comment.author.userId` to the caller, and `applyDeleteComment` (yorkie/comment-ops.ts:172-186) deletes the *entire thread* when index 0 is targeted. The product's own rule is author-only: `packages/frontend/src/components/comments/components/CommentThreadCard.tsx:89-92` gates edit/delete on `c.author.userId === currentUserId`, and no server-side equivalent exists anywhere (the CRDT was previously the only writer). Attack: member/API-key holder B calls `DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/<ws>/documents/<doc>/comments/<threadId>` with a thread id obtained from `GET .../comments`, silently erasing member A's review thread on a sheet, doc or PDF. The same controller also has no manager check, unlike `documents.controller.ts:191` which requires `isDocumentManager(...)` for the comparable destructive action (document delete). Mitigating context I confirmed: `yorkie-auth.controller.ts:195-206` states membership grants read+write with no viewer role, so a *JWT* member could already do this by writing the CRDT directly; the new surface makes it a first-class API operation and newly extends it to API keys, which cannot attach to Yorkie.

samples.summary: Worksheet image `src` is stored verbatim with no scheme or origin restriction, letting a member plant third-party/`javascript:`/`data:` URLs that every viewer of the sheet fetches
samples.evidence: `parseImages` validates only that `src` is a non-empty string (worksheet-images.ts:55 via `requireString`), and the controller comment states it is "kept verbatim". Every viewer of the tab then renders `` (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-object-layer.tsx:195-196) and `getOrLoadImage` issues the request, so `PUT .../tabs/:tabId/images` with `src: "https://attacker.example/beacon.png"` becomes an open-on-view beacon (viewer IP/UA/timing, including anonymous share-link viewers) inside a document the attacker may not own. `javascript:`/`data:` schemes are also accepted; both are inert in an ``, so I could not complete an XSS chain — hence medium confidence and minor severity. Verified NOT vulnerable: the share token is not leaked, because `appendShareTokenToImageUrl` refuses non-first-party origins (packages/frontend/src/api/share-image-url.ts:27-42), and the copy service classifies foreign refs rather than re-hosting them (packages/backend/src/document/document-image-refs.ts:33-34,113). No server-side fetch of `src` exists, so no SSRF.

samples.summary: Comments written through an API key are stored with `username: undefined`, so API-authored comments carry no usable author identity despite the docstring claiming otherwise
samples.evidence: `author()` (comments.controller.ts:100-108) builds `{ userId: String(req.user.id), username: req.user.username }`. For an API-key caller `req.user` is exactly `{ id, workspaceId, scopes, isApiKey }` — `ApiKeyStrategy.validate` (packages/backend/src/api-key/api-key.strategy.ts:22-27) never sets `username` or `photo` — so every thread/reply/`resolvedBy` created by a key persists an author record with an undefined username into the CRDT, which the editor's thread card renders as the author of record. The controller's own docstring (comments.controller.ts:74-77) asserts "an API key resolves to the user who minted it, which is the same identity the notification routes hold a comment reporter to", which holds for `userId` only. Impact is attribution/audit integrity of comments written by automation, not privilege escalation (the `userId` is correct, so the UI's author-only edit gate still resolves to the minter).

samples.summary: No size or count caps on the new CRDT writes (comment body, image collection, board elements), and Yorkie history is monotonic, so a member can permanently bloat a shared document
samples.evidence: `normalizeBody` (comment-ops.ts:203-207) accepts any string up to the global 25MB body limit (`packages/backend/src/main.ts:20,50`); `parseImages` caps neither the number of images nor `src` length (worksheet-images.ts:88-105); `assertValidBoardBody` walks `elements` with no length bound (docs-content.controller.ts:588-591). Each write goes into a Yorkie document whose history is retained, so a member or write-scoped key can repeatedly push near-limit payloads and make the document expensive or impossible for every editor to load. The sibling modules establish the limit pattern (`MaxAxisEntries`, `MaxClearedCells`, `MaxMergedCells` in packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-structure.ts:114,207,229 and worksheet-settings.ts:150), though `parseCharts` — the collection route this one mirrors — has no cap either, and the global `ThrottlerGuard` (app.module.ts:97,129) blunts the rate; hence low confidence that this is considered a gap.

samples.summary: Caller-controlled strings are used directly as object keys (`tabId` path param, `image.id`), with no rejection of `__proto__`/`constructor`
samples.evidence: `worksheetOrThrow` does `root.sheets?.[tabId]` (worksheet-images.controller.ts:55-60) with `tabId` straight from the URL, and `setImages` then assigns `ws.images[image.id] = image` (worksheet-images.controller.ts:106-107) with `image.id` an unconstrained caller string (`parseImages` only requires non-empty). On a plain object, a key of `__proto__` makes the lookup return `Object.prototype` (truthy, so the `NotFoundException` guard passes) and the subsequent `ws.images = {}` assignment would pollute the process-wide prototype; `constructor` similarly aliases an inherited member. At runtime both targets are Yorkie CRDT proxies, whose `get` resolves through the CRDT map and should return `undefined` for an absent key — I could not verify this because `@yorkie-js/sdk` is not installed in the working tree, hence low confidence. Defence-in-depth: reject `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` (or use a `Map`/`Object.create(null)`), as `shared-document.tsx:872-875` already does for the analogous API-supplied `type` lookup. `comment-ops.findThread` is safe by accident: it shape-checks `Array.isArray(thread.comments)` before use.
searchedFor: Glob '**/@yorkie-js/sdk/package.json' (SDK not installed — proxy get-handler unverifiable)

verdict.reason: Verified independently. The two delete handlers (comments.controller.ts:266-279 and :281-309) do not even inject @Req(), so no caller identity is available to compare against comment.author.userId; the only authorization is the document-in-workspace lookup in loadCommentableType (:92-95) plus the controller-level guards. workspace-scope.guard.ts:32-46 checks membership only (assertMember, no role inspection), and api-key-write-scope.guard.ts:38-49 checks only that an API key has the 'write' scope; api-v1.module.ts:48-77 registers no comment-specific guard and there is no global equivalent. comment-ops.ts:186-191 escalates a root-comment delete into deletion of the entire thread. A repo-wide search for ownership predicates (author, isAuthor, ownsComment/assertAuthor/canDeleteComment, 'userId ===' / 'userId !==') turned up ownership checks only at share-link.service.ts:61-62, analytics.controller.ts:170 and folders.controller.ts:85 - none on any comment path; the author-only rule lives solely client-side at CommentThreadCard.tsx:89-93, and comments.controller.spec.ts has no 403/author test. No counterexample exists. The mitigating context is real (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:193-206 shows membership grants rw on the document CRDT with no viewer tier, so a JWT member could already mutate comments through a Yorkie session) but it does not cover write-scoped API keys, which cannot attach to Yorkie and now receive a first-class targeted destructive operation on other members' threads, while the analogous destructive action in the same API surface (document delete) is gated on isDocumentManager. A missing ownership/manager gate on a destructive operation is squarely in the authorization lane, so the finding stays on the merge gate.
